clue.text: Meat finally stripped from bones into dishes

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the last letter of the word before is used
something stripped from a thing is taken away, so a letter leaves the word for the bones

blocks.note: the last letter of meat
patellas are kneecaps, bones of the knee

explanation.surface: A cook strips the last of the meat off the bones and puts it into dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Patellas are kneecaps; taking out their T leaves PAELLAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Paella is a Spanish rice dish cooked in a wide pan, so paellas are dishes.

clue.text: A singer abridged scales for consort

indicators.note: an abridged text is cut short, so the word for the singer loses its last letter
in a down clue, something that scales climbs, so it is read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a treble is a boy soprano, a singer

explanation.surface: A vocalist cut a few scales from the programme for the sake of a spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scales' looks like musical exercises after 'singer', but it means climbs: TREBL read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Albert was the husband and royal consort of Queen Victoria.

clue.text: Engineers jamming bug covertly

indicators.note: something jamming into a thing is squeezed inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a bug is an insect
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Technicians quietly blocking a listening device.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a standard crossword abbreviation; 'bug' points to spying but is just an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in secret means doing it hidden from others, which is what covertly means.

clue.text: Lover on the rebound posed first for make-up artist

indicators.note: a ball on the rebound comes back the way it went, so the word for posed runs backwards

blocks.note: a lover of something is a fan
a model posed, or sat, for a portrait
1st, written as IST

explanation.surface: A jilted lover, having modelled first, becomes a cosmetics professional.
explanation.walkthrough: A make-up artist here is someone who makes things up, not a beautician; 1st is read as IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantasist invents stories and lives in daydreams, so is literally an artist of making things up.

clue.text: Lament returning unfinished crossword?

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its end, so the final letter goes
returning means coming back, so the shortened word for lament is read backwards

blocks.note: a dirge is a lament for the dead

explanation.surface: A solver grumbles about handing back a puzzle left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a crossword is just one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword is set in a grid of squares, so the puzzle is an example of a grid.

clue.text: High grade heroin son is shooting up on the beach

indicators.note: the son shooting up rises to the top in this down clue, rearranging the slang word

blocks.note: A is the top grade
horse is slang for heroin
S, the son, is already in the slang word and moves to its top

explanation.surface: A drug-user's grim tale of a son injecting pure heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of HORSE moves up to the front, the top of a down entry, to make SHORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on land beside the sea, as when a sailor comes onto the beach.

clue.text: The One and Only? That’s music to try to reproduce

blocks.note: soul is a genre of music
animals mate when trying to breed

explanation.surface: A romantic insists that their song is the one and only, music to their ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The One' is the person you are meant to be with, and the wordplay neatly continues the romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A soulmate is a perfect partner, the person someone calls their one and only.

clue.text: Soviet aerial could be rusty?

blocks.note: the Soviets were the Reds
a satellite dish is an aerial

explanation.surface: An old Soviet antenna might have gone rusty.
explanation.walkthrough: Rust is reddish-brown, so 'could be' flags that rusty is one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rust has a red-brown colour, so a rusty shade is one kind of reddish colour.

clue.text: Finally beginning to set out for North American state capital

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, which is the one swapped out here
one letter is out and another is in for it, a straight swap

blocks.note: finally means at last
the first letter of set, which leaves
N is the compass abbreviation for North, which comes in
A is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: At last starting to head out for a capital city in North America.
explanation.walkthrough: AT LAST has its S swapped for N, then A for American is added to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlanta is the capital city of the US state of Georgia.

clue.text: Fix up men with drug on break

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece on another comes after it, so the men and drug are sent second

blocks.note: a break is a rest
OR, other ranks, are the ordinary soldiers or men
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: Mending soldiers who are on drugs during their leave.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword way to get ordinary soldiers from 'men'.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix up something old or damaged is to bring it back to a good state, to restore it.

clue.text: Wagnerian aria andof Tristan and Isolde strangely enthralling live?

indicators.note: the names are put strangely, in an odd order, so their letters are rearranged
to enthral is to hold captive, so the shuffled letters hold another piece inside

blocks.note: Tristan contributes his initial
taken as written
to live is to be, to exist

explanation.surface: The famous Wagner aria from Tristan and Isolde, oddly gripping when heard live.
explanation.walkthrough: The source text reads 'andof', apparently a typesetting slip; Tristan supplies only his initial.
explanation.definitionFit: The Liebestod, 'love-death', is Isolde's closing aria in Wagner's opera Tristan und Isolde.

clue.text: Naked yogi was positioned at the front to get stared at

indicators.note: naked means stripped of covering, so the outer letters of the next word are removed

blocks.note: the inner letters once the outer ones are stripped
someone who led was at the front of the field

explanation.surface: An unclothed yogi stood at the front of the class and drew stares.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle someone is to stare at them lecherously, so ogled means stared at.

clue.text: Star that’s behind Aries lit up sky briefly

indicators.note: the behind of a word is its rear end, so only its final letter is kept
said briefly, a word is cut short, losing its last letter
someone lit up is drunk, and the letters reel about into a new order

blocks.note: the final letter of that
taken as written
taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: An astrologer spots a star behind Aries lighting up the night sky.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word suggests astronomy, but the star wanted is the typographic symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An asterisk is the small star-shaped symbol used in printing.

clue.text: Beastly fare-dodgers, say, hiding in vehicles?

indicators.note: anything hiding in a place is tucked inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: vans are vehicles
e.g., for example, is what 'say' means

explanation.surface: Nasty passengers who skip paying for tickets, perhaps by hiding in vans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly fare' is food made from beasts and 'dodgers' avoid it; on the surface they are cheats on public transport.
explanation.definitionFit: Vegans avoid all animal products, so they dodge any food that comes from beasts.

clue.text: Teaches in fashion: it’s boring in the main

blocks.note: to drill pupils is to teach them by repetition
hip means fashionable

explanation.surface: A trendy teacher's lessons are, mostly, rather dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' means drilling holes and 'the main' is the open sea, not 'mostly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A drillship is a vessel fitted with a drilling rig to bore wells under the sea.

clue.text: Star act playing Ophelia exuding distress over tragedy?

indicators.note: to exude is to give off, so these letters ooze out of the name
actors playing take on new roles, so the letters take new places

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
to ail is to trouble or distress

explanation.surface: A leading actress playing a distraught Ophelia in the Hamlet tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: OPHELIA without the letters of AIL leaves OPHE to be mixed with STAR and ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: A catastrophe is a disaster, and in drama the term names the tragic final turn of events.

clue.text: Name originally invoked opening poetical epics?

definitions.text: Name originally invoked opening poetical epics?

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, so each of the following words gives only its first letter

blocks.note: to name someone is to call them
the initial letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Whose name was first called upon at the start of great epic poems?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: poets traditionally invoke the Muse at the opening of an epic.
explanation.definitionFit: Calliope is the Muse of epic poetry, the goddess an epic poet calls on in the first lines.

clue.text: He directs the news cycle?

blocks.note: surface reading: an editor who controls the round-the-clock flow of news
setter's reading: a lad who steers his bicycle round the streets carrying newspapers

explanation.surface: A media boss who sets the agenda of the news cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'news cycle' is a media phrase, but here it is the bike used to deliver the news.
explanation.definitionFit: The youngster delivering papers by bicycle literally directs, or steers, a cycle laden with news.

clue.text: City company restructured board

indicators.note: something restructured has been put together in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
taken as written

explanation.surface: A City firm reorganised its board of directors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' suggests London's financial district but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Córdoba is a historic city in Andalusia, Spain, and also a large city in Argentina.

clue.text: Bejewelled, perhaps, like Ronaldo’s boots?

blocks.note: first meaning: set with gems or ornaments
second meaning: fitted with studs for grip, as football boots are

explanation.surface: Were the footballer's flashy boots covered in jewels?
explanation.walkthrough: Cristiano Ronaldo is a footballer, and football boots have studs on the soles.
explanation.definitionFit: Studs can be jewelled ornaments or the grips on football boots, so one adjective serves both.

clue.text: Grease and fiddle with crude erection?

blocks.note: to grease is to oil
to fiddle or rig a result is to fix it dishonestly

explanation.surface: A smutty-sounding line about lubrication and fiddling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crude' is crude oil and 'erection' is a built structure, despite the innuendo.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil rig is a tall structure put up to extract crude oil from under the sea.

clue.text: Papers ignoring English cries for positive visions of the country

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out, so a letter is dropped from the cries

blocks.note: ID, identity papers
yells are loud cries
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Newspapers dismiss English protests in favour of rosy views of the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Idylls are idealised pictures of peaceful country life, as in pastoral poetry.

clue.text: Brazilian great coming back to plague United pulled out big game

indicators.note: coming back means going the other way, so the footballer's name runs backwards
a player pulled out is withdrawn, so that letter leaves the word

blocks.note: Pelé was Brazil's great footballer
to haunt is to plague or trouble persistently
U is the abbreviation for United

explanation.surface: A Brazilian legend returns to torment a United side that withdrew from a big match.
explanation.walkthrough: The football surface makes 'big game' look like a match, but it means large wild animals hunted for sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Big game is the large animals hunted on safari, and the elephant is the classic example.

clue.text: Camels might end up here then if hour is spent off course

indicators.note: something spent is used up and gone, so that letter disappears

blocks.note: Camel is a brand of cigarette, and stubbed-out cigarettes end up in this
h is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: Camels lose their way in the desert when an hour is wasted wandering.
explanation.walkthrough: The camels are cigarettes, not animals, which is why they end up in a receptacle.
explanation.definitionFit: Going astray means wandering away from the right path, being off course.

clue.text: Help District Attorney extracting volunteers from European country

indicators.note: extracting means drawing something out, so those letters are taken from the country

blocks.note: DA is the American abbreviation
Italy is a European country
the TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Assistance for a prosecutor who is extraditing volunteers from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily is British for a cleaner who comes in each day, so 'Help' is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic help who comes in each day to clean is known in Britain as a daily.

clue.text: Took balls from players and scored

blocks.note: the cast are the players in a show
to score something is to rate it

explanation.surface: A sports scene: someone took balls off the players and then scored.
explanation.walkthrough: The ball games are a decoy; the balls belong to an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To castrate is to remove the testicles, which slang calls balls.

clue.text: “Trump possibly is a scoundrel,” Republican admitted

indicators.note: someone admitted is let in, so this letter goes inside the other word

blocks.note: a cad is a scoundrel
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A political quote about a certain American president being a rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: Trump is not the politician but a trump, a card from the suit that beats the others.
explanation.definitionFit: A trump is a playing card of the winning suit, so a trump is one kind of card.

clue.text: Blair somehow seizing power over swinging state?

indicators.note: somehow means in some unexplained way, so the name's letters are rearranged
seizing means grabbing hold of, so the rearranged letters wrap round the rest

blocks.note: Tony Blair, taken as written
P is the abbreviation for power
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister grabs power in a swing state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swinging state' suggests a US swing state, but the swings are of mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Bipolar disorder is marked by swings between high and low moods, a swinging mental state.

clue.text: Very delayed after island gets cut off

indicators.note: after places the phrase meaning very delayed behind the island abbreviation, so it is sent second

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for island
so late means very delayed

explanation.surface: A long-delayed ferry leaves an island cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts SO LATE after I, though the clue names it first.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate something is to separate it from others, to cut it off.
